# Test fixtures generated by CMake

## Purpose

The Qwen3.6 port's parity tests compare engine kernels against dumps from the Python oracle
`ref/qwen36.py`, run on small synthetic qwen35moe GGUFs written by `tools/qwen36_synth_gguf.py`. Nothing is
checked in: the files are generated into the build directory at test time by CTest "fixture" steps. Four of
those steps are CMake scripts in `cmake/`, run as `cmake -DPYTHON=... -DSOURCE_DIR=... -DOUT=... -P <script>`;
four more call Python directly. This page covers the scripts, the interpreter probes, and the fixture chains.

Files covered:

| File | Lines |
| --- | ---: |
| [cmake/qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake](../../../cmake/qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake) | 27 |
| [cmake/qwen36_block_fixtures.cmake](../../../cmake/qwen36_block_fixtures.cmake) | 28 |
| [cmake/qwen36_oracle_dumps.cmake](../../../cmake/qwen36_oracle_dumps.cmake) | 35 |
| [cmake/qwen36_attn_fixtures.cmake](../../../cmake/qwen36_attn_fixtures.cmake) | 39 |
| the registrations in [CMakeLists.txt](../../../CMakeLists.txt) | `:239-260`, `:505-540`, `:674-716`, `:747-778`, `:803-816`, `:894-911` |

## The scripts

All four share a pattern: `file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${OUT})`, run Python with `-I` (isolated mode) through
`execute_process`, and on a missing dependency write `${OUT}/SKIP` (containing the error text) and `return()`
with status 0, because `cmake -P` cannot choose its exit code other than 1 for `FATAL_ERROR`
(`qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake:19`). Any other Python failure is a `FATAL_ERROR`. On success `${OUT}/SKIP` is
removed. The consuming test checks for `SKIP` and exits with its skip code.

| Script | Inputs | What it runs | Output in `${OUT}` | Skip detection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake` | `PYTHON`, `SOURCE_DIR`, `OUT` | `tools/qwen36_synth_gguf.py` four times: no flag, `--no-nextn`, `--fused-gate-up`, `--fused-qkv` (`:9-25`) | `toy.gguf`, `toy-nonextn.gguf`, `toy-fused-gate-up.gguf`, `toy-fused-qkv.gguf` | stderr matches `ModuleNotFoundError` (`:17`) |
| `qwen36_block_fixtures.cmake` | + `SYNTH` (the synth dir) | if `${SYNTH}/SKIP` or no `toy.gguf`: write SKIP and stop (`:9-13`); else `ref/qwen36.py ${SYNTH}/toy.gguf --tokens 104,101,108,108,111,32,119,111 --dump ${OUT}/o8` ("hello wo") | `o8/<seam>.f32`, `o8/manifest.txt` | `ModuleNotFoundError` (`:20`) |
| `qwen36_oracle_dumps.cmake` | `PYTHON`, `SOURCE_DIR`, `OUT` | `qwen36_synth_gguf.py k.gguf --gdn 2,4,128 --experts 256,8 --shexp-ff 512 --quant-shexp q8_0 --bf16-exact --no-nextn`; then `ref/qwen36.py` on the 11 tokens of "hello world" twice: F32 activations to `o_f32`, `--act-quant q8` to `o_q8` (`:16-32`) | `k.gguf`, `o_f32/`, `o_q8/`, `tokens.txt` | `ModuleNotFoundError` or `gguf-py was not found` (`:25`) |
| `qwen36_attn_fixtures.cmake` | `PYTHON`, `SOURCE_DIR`, `OUT` | for `g8` (16 q-heads / 2 kv, seed 3), `g12` (24 / 2, seed 5), `g2` (4 / 2, seed 11): `qwen36_synth_gguf.py <name>.gguf --heads H,KV --head-dim 256 --no-nextn --seed S`, then `ref/qwen36.py <name>.gguf --text "dense attention over sixteen heads, G=8!" --dump <name>-dump` (40 byte tokens) (`:14-37`) | `g8.gguf`, `g12.gguf`, `g2.gguf` and their `-dump/` dirs | `ModuleNotFoundError` or `gguf-py` in stdout/stderr (`:23`) |

Geometry notes from the script headers: `k.gguf` uses the GDN geometry the engine's CUDA GDN kernels are pinned
to (state 128, 2 k-heads / 4 v-heads, i.e. VPK 2 like the real 16 / 32), the real router shape (256 experts,
top-8) and the shared expert at its real width 512 in Q8_0; weights the engine reads as BF16 are made
BF16-representable. The attention fixtures cover the three query-heads-per-KV-head ratios the kernels are
built for: G = 8 (Qwen3.6), G = 12 (Flash-Next), G = 2 (the oracle's own GQA case).

## Python interpreter probes

| Variable | Line | Candidates (first with `import numpy` wins) | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_q36_python` | `:239-249` | `${Python3_EXECUTABLE}`, `<src>/.venv/bin/python`, `/usr/bin/python3`, `python3` | set only inside `if(STRATA_BUILD_TESTS)` |
| `_iq_python` | `:678-703` | `-DIQ_FIXTURE_PYTHON=...` alone if given; else `${Python3_EXECUTABLE}` (if found), `<src>/.venv/bin/python`, `<src>/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`, `/usr/bin/python3`, `python3` | any GPU build |

Without a numpy interpreter the dependent tests are not registered and a status line says so
(`:258-259`, `:713-715`).

## Fixture chains (CTest `FIXTURES_SETUP` / `FIXTURES_REQUIRED`)

```
qwen36_synth_fixtures ──(qwen36_synth_data)──> model_geometry_test            [skip 3]
          │
          └──> qwen36_block_fixtures ──(qwen36_block_data)──> qwen36_block_test [CUDA, skip 77]

qwen36_oracle_dumps   ──(qwen36_oracle_data)──> qwen36_seam_parity            [skip 77]
qwen36_attn_fixtures  ──(qwen36_attn_data)────> qsa_dense_parity --fixtures   [skip 77]

iq_parity_fixtures         (tools/iq_fixture.py, skip 3)                  ──> iq_parity        [skip 3]
prefill_qwen36_fixtures    (tests/python/qwen36_prefill_fixture.py, 1800 s) ──> prefill_qwen36_test (gdn3),
                                                                               prefill_qwen36_attn_test (full4)
qwen36_mtp_fixtures        (tests/python/qwen36_mtp_fixture.py, 1800 s)   ──> qwen36_mtp_test
qwen36_runner_fixtures     (tests/python/qwen36_runner_fixture.py, 1800 s) ──> qwen36_verify_test,
                                                                               qwen36_runner_check (runs `strata`)
```

The four Python fixtures set `STRATA_GGUF_PY=<src>/third_party/llama.cpp/gguf-py` in their environment
(`:533`, `:758`, `:775`); the `cmake -P` fixtures do not, and rely on `tools/_paths.py`'s default, which is
the same submodule path. Either way the gguf-py package comes from the llama.cpp submodule, so these fixtures
need `git submodule update --init`.

Output directories (all under the build dir): `qwen36_synth/`, `qwen36_block/`, `qwen36_oracle/`,
`qwen36_attn/`, `iq_fixture/`, `qwen36_prefill/`, `qwen36_mtp/`, `qwen36_runner/`.

## How the tests consume the outputs

- `model_geometry_test <dir>` returns 3 when `<dir>/SKIP` exists (`tests/core/model_geometry_test.cpp:263-266`).
- `qwen36_block_test` returns 77 on either `SKIP` or a missing `manifest.txt`
  (`tests/cuda/qwen36_block_test.cpp:209-211`).
- `qwen36_seam_parity` skips on `SKIP`, a missing `k.gguf` or a missing `o_f32/final_output-0.f32`
  (`src/kernels/qwen36_seam_parity.cpp:507`).
- `qsa_dense_parity --fixtures` skips on `SKIP` or a missing `g8.gguf` (`src/kernels/qsa_dense_parity.cpp:606`).

## Gotchas

- **Missing gguf-py fails instead of skipping in two scripts.** When the submodule is not checked out,
  `tools/_paths.py:21` exits with "llama.cpp's gguf-py was not found: run setup.py ..." (exit 1, no
  `ModuleNotFoundError`). `qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake` and `qwen36_block_fixtures.cmake` match only
  `ModuleNotFoundError`, so they hit `FATAL_ERROR`, the fixture test fails and its dependants are Not Run.
  Verified here: with an empty `third_party/llama.cpp`, `qwen36_synth_fixtures` fails and `model_geometry_test`
  is Not Run. The other two scripts also match the gguf-py message and skip correctly. (The `setup.py` named in
  the message was removed in this fork.)
- The header comments of `qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake:5`, `qwen36_block_fixtures.cmake:7` and
  `qwen36_oracle_dumps.cmake:12` say "Exit 3"; the scripts actually exit 0 and leave the `SKIP` marker; the
  consuming test produces the skip code.
- `cmake_policy(SET CMP0007 NEW)` in `qwen36_synth_fixtures.cmake:6` is required for the `"toy.gguf;"` case on
  CMake < 4 (CMake 3.31 dropped the empty element and `list(GET 1)` failed; fixed in commit `cd2a73c` per
  [pascal-build.md](../../qwen36-port/pascal-build.md)).
- In a GPU build without `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS`, `qwen36_oracle_dumps` and `qwen36_attn_fixtures` are registered
  with an empty `PYTHON` because `_q36_python` is undefined there (see
  [test-targets.md](test-targets.md#gotchas)).
